title: Stabilize scheduler jitter to rescue high-frequency short flows across hosting modes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers (Hosted + Dedicated + Private) escalated intermittent severe tail latency for small requests during mixed-length workloads. Investigation shows the continuous-batching admission jitter logic can oscillate under microburst patterns and minor clock drift, starving short requests and creating long-context tail spikes. This ticket implements a stabilizing patch, tests, and a staged rollout path.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run a mixed-length workload: 80% short requests (prompt length < 64 tokens) at 1k qps and 20% long-context inference (prompt length 8k+) interspersed at 1-2% microbursts.
2) Use default continuous-batching config with jitter_enabled=true and adaptive_window=true.
3) Observe a progressive suppression of short-request throughput and 95/99/999 latency spikes aligning with batch window oscillations.
4) Reproduce under Hosted and Dedicated modes; in Private, reproduce by toggling upgrade window to force maintenance scheduling overlap.
root_cause_summary: A confluence bug: the admission jitter timer interacts poorly with adaptive window resizing and the KV-cache eviction path. Microbursts cause the scheduler to contract and expand the admission window rapidly; small clock skew across host nodes and preemptive kernel selection amplify oscillation. Eviction-triggered backpressure briefly blocks prefetch, which allows the oscillation to persist and starve short flows until hysteresis is broken.
mitigation_plan: Hotfix v1: disable jitter scaling under mixed-length detection (immediate workaround) — deploy to Hosted as a hotpatch (runtime-1.19.hotfix)

Short-term fix: add admission-smoothing with time-based hysteresis (minimum stable window duration = 250ms) and a shortflow reservation token (5% of inflight slots) to guarantee progress for tiny requests.
Long-term fix: separate admission controller for KV-sensitive requests, add NTP-guard checks for drift > 50ms and make prefetch handshake idempotent to avoid eviction/backpressure races.
Add monitoring and automated rollback triggers if 99p latency for short flows increases by >20% post-rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Hotpatch): Hosted - immediate rollout to 10% of runtime-1.19 fleet (hotfix tag), monitor 5m cadence metrics and customer-facing SLOs.
Phase 1 (Canary): runtime-1.20 canary in Hosted (single AZ) for 24h with load generator reproducer (see tests) — if green, advance.
Phase 2: Dedicated - schedule staged wave across committed clusters (low-traffic windows), enable shortflow reservation toggle and observe per-tenant latency.
Phase 3: Private - ship patch and docs for customer ops; provide migration notes for on-prem upgrade window; offer assisted upgrade for customers who reported the escalation.
Phase 4: Full rollout with automated rollback on threshold breach.
Notify SC/TP and Customer Success at each phase start + post-mortem publish.
tests: Deterministic load test: mixed-length generator that reproduces the oscillation sequence used by the incident (seeded traffic pattern).
Chaos test: inject KV-eviction delays and clock skew up to 80ms between hosts during load to validate hysteresis guards.
E2E latency test: measure 50/95/99/999 quantiles for small requests and long-context requests separately under identical traffic blends.
Regression: ensure batching throughput does not degrade >5% for heavy long-context workloads after shortflow reservation is enabled.
telemetry_queries: Hosted: SELECT histogram(99) FROM runtime_request_latency WHERE model IN (...) AND tokens < 64 GROUP BY tenant, 1m
KV evictions: count(kv_eviction_events) by host over 5m windows — correlate with shortflow latency spikes
Per-tenant small-request SLO breach: COUNT_IF(latency>150ms AND tokens<64)/total_short_reqs > 0.2 on 5m window -> trigger rollback

2026-03-02 - Marcus Chen: Confirmed reproduction in staging with mixed-length generator. Observed window size oscillation correlated with 99/999 spikes for short flows.

2026-03-08 - QA (Priya Nair): Chaos tests passed for jitter-disabled hotfix but flagged regression in long-context tail at 99p for a narrow model family. Added canary guard to rollout plan.

Action items: finish documentation for Private upgrade notes, coordinate Dedicated cluster wave scheduling with Ops, publish customer communications template.
acceptance_criteria: Incident reproducer no longer creates progressive short-request starvation in 10 consecutive runs.
After runtime-1.20 rollout, 99p latency for tokens<64 improves to baseline (pre-incident) within 10% margin for Hosted and Dedicated.
Private deployment customers have clear upgrade path and can opt into admission smoothing via toggle; no data plane incompatibilities.
Monitoring alerts and automated rollback defined and exercised in canary.
notes: We intentionally keep the shortflow reservation small (5%) to limit impact on long-context throughput and committed capacity economics.
This ticket ties into longer term work on per-tenant admission controllers (project: per-tenant-guardrails). Consider splitting heavy refactor into follow-up epic.
Coordinate with Product on customer communications and with Sales for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private assisted upgrades.
